title: lua_run_http runs an HTTP error page as a script and reports success, although the docs promise err on an error response
claim: The docs say `err` fires for 'a lua_run_http request that fails at the HTTP layer', and the example comment says err means 'the endpoint was unreachable or returned an error response'. LuaRunHTTP never checks resp.StatusCode. A 404 or 500 body is loaded and run as Lua, and the result is `{ok: true}` with a null err. Verifier: As stated. A non-2xx body that is not valid Lua, such as an HTML error page, comes back as ok=false, a script error, rather than as err. So the documented transport-error branch never fires for an HTTP error status.
evidence: lua.go:59-70: `resp, err := httpClient.Get(url.Value) ... body, err := io.ReadAll(resp.Body) ... return resultAndError(runLuaSource(string(body), ...), nil)`, with no status check. Test builtin/zz_doc2_test.go TestZZDoc2LuaHTTPStatus: an httptest server answering 404 with body `return "allow"` gives `lua_run_http on 404 -> {error: , ok: true, result: allow, schema_version: 1}`. The ledger mentions the status check only inside M26-TOOL-012's fix_proposal ('Also check resp.StatusCode, since today a 404 page is loaded as Lua'). No row holds it as a defect or records that the documentation promises the opposite. Verifier: builtin/zz_verify_test.go TestZZLuaHTTP404: an httptest server answering 404 or 500 with the body `return "allow"` gave `{error: , ok: true, result: allow, schema_version: 1}` with no err. lua.go:59-70 never reads resp.StatusCode. RUNTIME_INTEGRATION.md:30-33 and the example comment at :246-249 promise err when the endpoint 'returned an error response'. Verifier's notes: Not a duplicate of M26-TOOL-012. That row is the unbounded io.ReadAll; this one is the missing status check against a documented promise. The two share a line, and the fix can land together.
repro: go1.26.2 test ./builtin -run ZZDoc2LuaHTTPStatus -v (scratch tree)
impact: A policy endpoint that returns an error page, or a proxy or captive-portal page, is either run as policy or reported as a script error instead of a transport error. The documented fallback path ('if err, fall back to a local default') never triggers.
fix_proposal: Refuse a non-2xx status with an err naming the status, before Load. Fold this into the TOOL-012 LimitReader change. Regression test: TestLuaRunHTTPRefusesNon2xx: an httptest 404 whose body is valid Lua must return a non-null err and no result.

title: BYTECODE_IR says continue jumps to the loop condition; the compiler sends it to the post section
claim: Section 13.2 says `Patch all continuePositions -> conditionStart address (re-runs the condition check, which then falls through to the post-increment)`. A continue patched to the condition would skip `i = i + 1` and loop forever. The code patches continue to the start of the post section. Section 13.1's pseudocode also leaves out the OpPop the compiler emits after the post expression.
evidence: compiler.go:1786-1790: `postStartPosition := len(c.currentInstructions()) ... for _, pos := range ctx.continuePositions { c.changeOperand(pos, postStartPosition) }`, then `c.emit(code.OpPop)` after Post at :1802. Disassembly of `for (let i = 0; i < 3; i = i + 1) { if (i == 1) { continue; } let z = i; }` (compiler/zz_doc2_test.go): the condition starts at 0006, the continue is `0026 OpJump 41`, the post starts at `0041 OpGetGlobal 0`, and `0054 OpPop` precedes `0055 OpJump 6`. Verifier: compiler/zz_verify_test.go disassembly of `for (let i = 0; i < 3; i = i + 1) { if (i == 1) { continue; } let z = i; }`: the condition starts at 0006, continue is `0026 OpJump 41`, the post section starts at `0041 OpGetGlobal 0`, and `0054 OpPop` comes before `0055 OpJump 6`. compiler.go:1786-1790 patches continuePositions to postStartPosition. BYTECODE_IR.md:1144-1148 says conditionStart. Verifier's notes: This is an internals document and does not affect users, so priority is lowered to P3.
repro: go1.26.2 test ./compiler -run ZZDoc2Disasm -v (scratch tree)
impact: A contributor who follows the IR reference for loop codegen would build an infinite-loop bug. This is an internals document, so users are not affected.
fix_proposal: In 13.2, patch continue to the post section in a for loop and to the condition in while and for-in, which the while comment at compiler.go:1719-1725 already explains. Add the trailing OpPop after [post] in 13.1. Regression test: A docs test that compiles the section 13.1 loop and asserts the continue target equals the post-section offset. Or delete the prose claim.

title: BYTECODE_IR's listings and tables disagree with the encoder and VM (struct literal, OpGetBuiltin width, stack notation, ByteCode fields)
claim: (1) Section 11.2 compiles `Point { x: 1, y: 2 }` as `OpConstant <idx of "Point"> ; push type name string` before the fields. The compiler emits no such push, and if it did, OpMakeStruct would leave it on the stack. (2) The section 9.3 table gives OpGetBuiltin an IP advance of `+1`, but its operand is 2 bytes (section 3.1 and code.go:147) and the VM advances `ip += 2`. (3) Section 3.2 says the stack column is 'listed bottom-first (so `b, a` means `a` is on top)', but the table is written top-first: `OpIndex idx, obj` read bottom-first would put obj on top, while the VM pops index first. (4) The section 4 ByteCode struct omits ModuleSpans and GlobalNames.
evidence: compiler.go:2266-2279 does `typeNameIndex := c.addConstant(...)`, compiles only the field expressions, then `c.emit(code.OpMakeStruct, typeNameIndex, len(typeDef))`. Disassembly: `0000 OpConstant 1 / 0003 OpConstant 2 / 0006 OpMakeStruct 0 2 / 0010 OpSetGlobal 0`. vm.go:1093-1103: OpGetBuiltin reads `vm.readUint16(ins, ip+1)` and then `vm.currentFrame().ip += 2`. vm.go:1220-1222: `case code.OpIndex: index := vm.pop(); left := vm.pop()`. compiler.go:161 `ModuleSpans []ModuleSpan` and :174 `GlobalNames []string` are missing from the doc's struct. Verifier: Disassembly of `Point { x: 1, y: 2 }`: `OpConstant 1 / OpConstant 2 / OpMakeStruct 0 2 / OpSetGlobal 0`, with no type-name push (compiler.go:2266-2279). code.go:147 declares OpGetBuiltin with operand width 2, and vm.go advances ip += 2. Doc table :869 says +1. The doc's OpSub row `b, a -> a-b` with 'bottom-first (a on top)' contradicts the VM popping the right operand first (OpIndex: vm.go pops index, then left), so the listing is actually top-first. ModuleSpans and GlobalNames exist at compiler.go:161/174 and are missing from the doc's section 4 struct.
repro: go1.26.2 test ./compiler -run ZZDoc2Disasm -v (scratch tree). Read vm.go:1093-1103 and 1220-1222.
impact: A reader who hand-assembles or disassembles bytecode from this reference gets wrong stack effects and widths.
fix_proposal: Drop the OpConstant line in 11.2, change OpGetBuiltin to +2 in 9.3, change 3.2 to 'listed top-first (`b, a` means b is on top)', and add the two fields to section 4. Regression test: none (prose). Optionally a docs test that recompiles the 11.2 and 10.1 snippets and compares them with the listing.

title: BYTECODE_IR's runtime and security sections contradict the code and each other (vm.New secure mode, the marker, ReadUint16, crypto/rand placement)
claim: (1) Section 15.3 says '`secureMode = false` for plain `vm.New`'. vm.New sets secureMode true, and the doc's own section 18 table says true. (2) Section 16.6 says the marker 'is encrypted together with the rest of the bytecode' and that DetectPolymorphicLevel detects it. Section 15.6 says generator.encode strips it before anything is written, and polymorphic.go says the heuristic must never be used for that. (3) Sections 2.5, 14.2 and 19-P1 teach code.ReadUint16/ReadUint8 as 'the only correct way during execution'. The VM never calls them: it has cached-stream readers, and the code functions have no caller (M26-CMP-014). (4) Section 6.6 says injection placement 'uses crypto/rand'. Every generator build seeds it.
evidence: vm.go:189-227: New(...) sets `secureMode: true`. compiler/polymorphic.go:665-679: 'So it must never be used to decide whether to truncate ... Ask the compiler instead'. generator/generate.go:306 comment: 'This used to call DetectPolymorphicLevel'. vm.go:631-656: `readUint16 and readUint8 ... are the cached-stream equivalents of code.ReadUint16/code.ReadUint8`. generate.go:210 `comp.SetSecurityCheckSeed(resolvePolymorphismSeed(mutationSeed))`. Verifier: vm.go:227 New() sets `secureMode: true`, while BYTECODE_IR.md:1342 says false. generate.go:300-312 strips the marker by mutation level and explains that DetectPolymorphicLevel was abandoned, while doc 16.6 says the marker is encrypted with the bytecode and detected. `grep code.ReadUint16|code.ReadUint8` finds only a comment at vm.go:632 (M26-CMP-014), yet doc :144-159 calls them 'the only correct way'. generate.go:210 always calls SetSecurityCheckSeed, and compiler.go:469 says crypto/rand is used only when no seed is set, yet doc :543 says 'uses crypto/rand'. Verifier's notes: The dead-API half is the doc side of M26-CMP-014. The finding is kept because the defect is in the document.
repro: Read the cited lines side by side, and `grep -rn 'code.ReadUint16\|code.ReadUint8' --include=*.go vm compiler`, which finds only a comment.
impact: A maintainer following the 'critical rule' calls a dead, slower API. A reader of 15.3 believes the default VM is lenient on tamper when it halts.
fix_proposal: Fix 15.3 to match section 18. Rewrite 16.6 as 'the marker is appended and then stripped by generator.encode; DetectPolymorphicLevel is test-only'. Point 2.5, 14.2 and P1 at VM.readUint16/readUint8. Say in 6.6 that the seeded RNG is used when a seed is set, which the generator always does. Regression test: none (prose)

title: LSP extension LLD and onboarding describe server selection, hover fallback, registry rules and formatter behaviour the code no longer has
claim: (1) LLD 9.1 says that without `mutant.languageServer.path` the extension searches workspace roots for the newest mlsp. The code first uses the binary bundled in the VSIX (`bin/mlsp-<os>-<arch>`), which wins over any workspace build. The onboarding tells a new engineer to 'Confirm the latest local mlsp binary is being selected', which it is not. (2) LLD 8 describes a 'Prefix-based fallback for builtin families (fs_, db_, bytes_, http_)' and a 'Generic fallback for any builtin registered', and says new builtins get 'baseline hover/signature coverage' automatically. No fallback exists: without a builtinDocs entry there is no card. (3) LLD 12.2 says to register a builtin 'append-only'. CONTRIBUTING and builtin.go say the order is no longer ABI. (4) Onboarding Option 2 says 'optionally add rich docs in language_teach.go'. builtinDocs lives in builtin/metadata.go and is required. (5) LLD 14 and onboarding Exercise C and section 9 describe 'preservation-first' formatting for documents with comments or blank lines. LLD 6 and the formatter say comments go through the AST printer and the code is rewritten. (6) 'Seven rules' heads a list of eight security rules. (7) LLD 9.3 omits the Mutant: Format Document command. Verifier: Right except for the fallback sub-claim. A prefix-family table does exist: builtinFamilyDocs/TeachingFamilySummary at builtin/metadata.go:3028-3145. It is wired only into REPL help (repl_help.go:511), not into LSP hover or signature help. So the LSP has no fallback, as claimed, but 'no prefix table exists' is imprecise.
evidence: extension.ts:250-259: `if (trimmedConfigured.length > 0) return trimmedConfigured; const bundledServerPath = resolveBundledLanguageServerPath(...); if (bundledServerPath) return bundledServerPath;` comes before findLatestServerBinary. hover_card.go:338-342: `signature, summary, params, ok := builtin.TeachingDoc(name); if !ok { return callableCard{}, false }`, and metadata.go:3074-3078 returns false when there is no builtinDocs entry. language_teach.go contains no prefix table. builtin.go:366: 'This list's order is no longer part of the ABI'. CONTRIBUTING.md:271-272. metadata.go:387 `var builtinDocs`. server_test.go:2417-2476 expects `let   answer=1;` beside comments to become `let answer = 1;`. The LLD 5 security list names tlsVerificationDisabled, unboundedResource, weakCrypto, hardcodedSecret, commandInjection, evidenceMutation, classifiedPlaintext and pathTraversal, which is 8. package.json:216-217 has `mutant.formatDocument`. Verifier: extension.ts:250-259 returns resolveBundledLanguageServerPath before the workspace search, which LLD 9.1 omits. hover_card.go:338-342 returns no card when TeachingDoc fails. LLD :553 says append-only, while builtin.go:366 and CONTRIBUTING.md:272 say the order is not ABI. The onboarding points rich docs at language_teach.go, but builtinDocs is in builtin/metadata.go. server_test.go expects `let   answer=1;` next to comments to become `let answer = 1;`, not preserved. LLD 'Seven rules' lists 8 (the eighth is pathTraversal). package.json:216 defines mutant.formatDocument, which is missing from LLD 9.3. Verifier's notes: The formatter's comment-moving behaviour is M26-LSP-020, a separate defect.
repro: Read the cited lines. extension.ts resolveLanguageServerCommandFromInputs.
impact: An engineer onboarding with these documents debugs the wrong binary (a stale bundled server wins over the one they just built), looks for a fallback that does not exist, and follows a registry rule that no longer applies.
fix_proposal: Insert the bundled-binary step into 9.1 and the onboarding troubleshooting. Replace the fallback bullets with 'every builtin must have a builtinDocs entry (meta-test)'. Remove 'append-only'. Point Option 2 at builtin/metadata.go. Delete LLD 14's first bullet and the preservation language in the onboarding. Change 'Seven' to 'Eight' and add Format Document. Regression test: none (prose)

title: WASM REPL reference gives stale counts, wrong truthiness and a usage example that fails
claim: (1) The quick reference says the browser-safe set is '238 of 459'. It is 325 of 659, and the same doc's section 5 says 659. (2) Section 3.3 lists 'empty or whitespace-only string' as falsy. A whitespace-only string is truthy. (3) The section 9.3 example fails: `putln(cache_get("session", "count")["value"])` raises 'index operator not supported: MULTI_VALUE', and `putln(len(db_query_nodes(h)))` prints an error because db_query_nodes returns a (value, err) pair. (4) Section 3.2 promises an 'explicit unsupported syntax error', a path that no longer exists now that the REPL runs the real compiler. (5) Section 11 tells maintainers to 'Update webrepl/repl.go supported builtin registry and wrappers'. The set is derived in browser_safe.go and there is no registry to update. Verifier: As stated. More of the 9.3 example fails than the auditor listed: `let h = db_open()` binds the pair, so db_add_node/db_add_edge fail as well. The cached 7 comes back as 7.000000, which is M26-BLT-010.
evidence: webrepl/zz_doc2_test.go on webrepl.New(): `total=659 safe=325 categories=41`. `if ("  ") {...}` gives out="ws-truthy", and `if ("")` gives "empty-falsy". The cache example gives err=`index operator not supported: MULTI_VALUE`. The db example gives out="ERROR:argument to `len` not supported, got MULTI_VALUE at 5:7". webrepl/repl.go:81-139 Eval has no 'unsupported syntax' branch. browser_safe.go:10-16 documents the derivation. Verifier: webrepl/zz_verify_test.go on webrepl.New(): total=659, safe=325, against the doc's '238 of 459'. `if ("  ")` gives ws-truthy. `putln(cache_get("session","count")["value"])` gives err 'index operator not supported: MULTI_VALUE'. In the 9.3 db block, `db_add_edge(h,n1,n2)` returns an ERROR (argument 1 got MULTI_VALUE), and `putln(len(db_query_nodes(h)))` prints 'argument to `len` not supported, got MULTI_VALUE'. An illegal token gives the ordinary parser error 'no prefix parse function for ILLEGAL', with no 'unsupported syntax' path (repl.go:81-139). The doc's section 11 names a registry that is derived in browser_safe.go.
repro: go1.26.2 test ./webrepl -run ZZDoc2Wasm -v (scratch tree)
impact: A browser-REPL user copying section 9.3 gets errors. The truthiness table predicts the wrong branch for whitespace strings.
fix_proposal: Generate or fix the count (325 of 659), and remove 'whitespace-only' from the falsy list. Rewrite 9.3 with `let got, err = cache_get(...); putln(got["value"])` and `let ids, err = db_query_nodes(h); putln(len(ids))`. Delete the unsupported-syntax line and point section 11 at browser_safe.go. Regression test: A webrepl test that evaluates each section 9 snippet and asserts no error. Tag the fences `mutant` so D1 compiles them.

title: INTERCHANGE_SCHEMAS' supertimeline and STIX examples fail as written
claim: The supertimeline example `timeline_merge([events_from(...), ..., events_from(...),\n]);` fails twice. A trailing comma before `]` is a parse error, although a trailing comma before `}` in a hash is accepted. With the comma removed, timeline_merge refuses the elements, because each events_from call yields a (value, err) MULTI_VALUE. The STIX example `extract_iocs(fs_read("report.txt"))` fails the same way, because fs_read returns a pair. The fences are untagged, so the D1 compile check never sees them.
repro: PowerShell in the scratch tree: .\mutant.exe run zz\i1.mut --password-file pw.txt; .\mutant.exe zz\i1.mu --dev --password-file pw.txt (and zz\tc1.mut, zz\tc2.mut)
impact: The document's headline pattern, one merge building a supertimeline, does not run. A reader has to discover the pair-unwrapping on their own.
fix_proposal: Bind each events_from result (`let a, e1 = events_from(...);`) and merge the names. Drop the trailing comma, or make parseExpressionList accept a trailing comma as the hash parser does. Bind fs_read before extract_iocs. Tag the fences `mutant` so D1 compiles them (it would have caught the parse error). Regression test: Tag the fences and let D1 compile them. Add a parser test for a trailing comma in array literals, whichever way that is decided.

title: RUNTIME_INTEGRATION's make_scorer example fails: string + integer is not supported
claim: The example builds Lua source with `"local bytes = " + bytes_seen + ...` where bytes_seen is 20480. Mutant refuses STRING + INTEGER, so the program stops with a VM error before any Lua runs.
evidence: zz/lua1.mut (the doc's two examples verbatim, second result renamed) printed `risk score:  30` for the first example. Then: `vm_runtime_error ip=5 op=OpAdd: ... unsupported types for binary operation: STRING, INTEGER`, traceback `at make_scorer(bytes_seen=20480, connections=6) (zz\lua1.mut:14:18)`. Verifier: zz/lua.mut holds the doc's make_scorer example verbatim. Running it gave 'vm_runtime_error ip=5 op=OpAdd: ... unsupported types for binary operation: STRING, INTEGER', with a traceback at make_scorer(bytes_seen=20480, connections=6) line 2.
repro: PowerShell in the scratch tree: .\mutant.exe run zz\lua1.mut --password-file pw.txt; .\mutant.exe zz\lua1.mu --dev --password-file pw.txt
impact: The document's example of passing inputs into a Lua scorer crashes when copied.
fix_proposal: Use interpolation (`"local bytes = ${bytes_seen}; ..."`) or to_string(). Tag the fence `mutant` so D1 compiles it. Regression test: Tag the fences `mutant`. Optionally add the example to examples/lua with a golden.

title: GRAPH_DATABASE says no builtin compacts a store and that hash index-assignment is unsupported; both are false
claim: The Notes bullet says 'Disk compaction has no script-level trigger ... no db_* builtin performs it from mutant code'. Section 5 of the same document introduces db_compact, which does exactly that. Lines 160-162 and 388-389 tell readers to build their ID index with `set` 'since index-assignment on an existing hash value is not supported'. `h[k] = v` works (OpSetIndex, and the WASM summary lists 'index and field assignment'). The capability table gives db_open_disk as `(path)`, leaving out the new opts hash (memory_budget, discover_memory_budget, verify_on_open). Verifier: As stated. The doc contradicts itself on compaction.
evidence: builtin/names.go registers db_compact. zz/g2.mut: `let h = {}; h["k"] = 1; putln("index assign: ", h);` printed `index assign:  {k: 1}`. `db_compact(db)` on an in-memory handle returned `{delta_records_after: 0, delta_records_before: 0, has_storage: false}`. metadata.go:2187 `db_open_disk(path, opts?)`. The doc's full 'Putting it together' program runs as written (zz/g1.mut: 3 nodes, 2 edges, hops 1, closed cleanly). Verifier: GRAPH_DATABASE.md:393-397 says no db_* builtin compacts, but the same document's :35 and :255-264 introduce db_compact (names.go:295). zz/g2.mut: `h["k"] = 1` prints {k: 1}, and db_compact on an in-memory handle returns {delta_records_after: 0, delta_records_before: 0, has_storage: false}. metadata.go:2187 gives `db_open_disk(path, opts?)`, but the doc table :23 says `(path)`.
repro: PowerShell in the scratch tree: .\mutant.exe run zz\g2.mut --password-file pw.txt; .\mutant.exe zz\g2.mu --dev --password-file pw.txt
impact: Readers are told a maintenance action they need does not exist, and are steered away from ordinary hash assignment.
fix_proposal: Delete or rewrite the last Notes bullet so it points at db_compact. Replace the `set` advice with `ip_index["192.168.1.4"] = ip_node;`. Add opts? to the db_open_disk row. Regression test: none (prose) Fixed: The Notes bullet now points at db_compact, the `set` advice is replaced by index assignment and db_find, and the capability table lists every db_* builtin with its declared signature, held there by the new test.

title: CONTRIBUTING describes three gob registration lists and says there is no .gitattributes; there is one list and a .gitattributes exists
claim: 'Bytecode format changes touch three separate gob registration lists -- runner/runner.go, generator/generate.go and compiler/linetable_test.go. Missing one means an artifact that fails to round-trip.' The three were merged into serialize/gobtypes.go, and all three sites now call serialize.RegisterGobTypes(). The Windows note says 'the repository has no .gitattributes'. It has one, which marks examples/data/** -text. Verifier: Both halves hold. The substance of the Windows note still stands, because .gitattributes covers only examples/data/** and Go files still follow core.autocrlf. Only the literal 'no .gitattributes' is false.
evidence: serialize/gobtypes.go:1-8: 'The list used to be written out three times -- in the generator, in the runner, and in a compiler test -- and it drifted'. generator/generate.go:318, runner/runner.go:331 and compiler/linetable_test.go:185 all call `serialize.RegisterGobTypes()`. `git ls-files` lists .gitattributes, whose content is `examples/data/** -text`. Verifier: CONTRIBUTING.md:187-189 names three gob lists. Instead, serialize/gobtypes.go:69 RegisterGobTypes() is called from generator/generate.go:318, runner/runner.go:331, compiler/linetable_test.go:185 and mutil/util.go:352,362. CONTRIBUTING.md:225 says there is no .gitattributes, but `git ls-files .gitattributes` lists it with `examples/data/** -text`. Verifier's notes: The gob-list half is the same defect as ARCH.05 (CONTRIBUTING.md:181-189), which also covers the evaluator/REPL misstatement. The .gitattributes half is new. Fold one into the other when merging.
repro: grep -rn 'RegisterGobTypes\|gob.Register(' --include=*.go . ; git -C O:/project/mutant ls-files .gitattributes
impact: A contributor changing the container edits three call sites looking for a list that is not there, and misses the one file that matters.
fix_proposal: Point the rule at serialize.GobTypes. Reword the Windows note: '.gitattributes covers only the evidence fixtures, so Go files still follow core.autocrlf'. Regression test: none (prose)

title: The release gate's fuzz step writes into the working tree, although the gate promises it never does
claim: The script header and the changelog say 'nothing is written into the working tree -- builds, logs and scratch copies go under --log-dir'. With --fuzz-time set, the fuzz step runs `go test -fuzz` in each package. When a target fails, Go writes the failing input to <package>/testdata/fuzz/<Target>/<hash>, inside the checkout. Verifier: Latent only. The promise that nothing is written into the tree holds at 7aeee5a because there are no fuzz targets (LIM.02). It will break the first time a fuzz target is added and fails under --fuzz-time.
evidence: release_gate.sh:130: `run "$log" env CGO_ENABLED=0 "$GO" test -run '^$' -fuzz "^$target\$" -fuzztime "$FUZZ_TIME" "$pkg"`, run with the repository as the working directory (line 36 `cd "$REPO_ROOT"`). Repro in the scratch copy: a failing FuzzZZ in zzfuzz/ run with `-fuzz ^FuzzZZ$ -fuzztime 20s` left `zzfuzz/testdata/fuzz/FuzzZZ/06ba4bdb19de593e` in the tree. Verifier: In the scratch tree, a failing FuzzZZ run with `go1.26.2 test -run '^$' -fuzz '^FuzzZZ$' -fuzztime 10s ./zzfuzz` left zzfuzz/testdata/fuzz/FuzzZZ/06ba4bdb19de593e. release_gate.sh at HEAD runs that command from REPO_ROOT (cd at :36) for every Fuzz* target listed. However, `git grep -E 'func Fuzz' HEAD -- *.go` finds nothing, so at HEAD the step always prints 'SKIP: no fuzz targets' and cannot write.
repro: go1.26.2 test -run '^$' -fuzz '^FuzzZZ$' -fuzztime 20s ./zzfuzz; find zzfuzz -type f (scratch tree)
impact: The file appears exactly when the gate fails. It is an untracked file in the checkout, which the next gofmt_lf pass also picks up. Usually this is wanted (a reproducer), but it is not what the gate says it does.
fix_proposal: Either state the exception ('a failing fuzz target leaves its reproducer under testdata/fuzz, as go test does'), or run fuzzing in a scratch copy under --log-dir and copy the reproducer path into the log. Regression test: none

title: DETECTION_RULES tells readers to store a rule with case_add_evidence, which is not a builtin
claim: 'a rule can be printed, stored in a case with `case_add_evidence`, or diffed'. No builtin has that name. The case family is case_open, case_note, case_evidence, case_verify, case_manifest, case_write, case_manifest_verify, case_report, case_bundle and case_close. The rest of the document checked out: the eight refusal rows each produced their named error (builtin/zz_doc2_test.go TestZZDoc2Sigma), and examples/detection/sigma_rules.golden matches the sample output apart from indentation. Verifier: `git grep case_add_evidence HEAD` finds it only at docs/DETECTION_RULES.md:49. names.go:616-632 registers case_open/note/evidence/verify/manifest/write/manifest_verify/report/bundle/close and case_key_*, and none of them is case_add_evidence.
repro: grep -n 'case_add_evidence' builtin/names.go

title: HOME/USERPROFILE picked the signing key and the --signer-auth trust anchor, although the docs said the command line fully determines a run
claim: The docs say no environment variable is obeyed, that the invocation and the artifact together fully determine the behaviour (SECURITY_RUNBOOK 4), that the key directory is `<home>/.mutant/keys`, 'fixed' (BINARY_ARTIFACT_SECURITY_DEEP_DIVE 3), and that section 5 of SECURITY_LLD_TRACEABILITY is 'the complete control surface'. ResolveLocalKeyStoreDir called os.UserHomeDir(), which reads USERPROFILE on Windows and $HOME on Unix. That directory holds the key that signs every .mu artifact, case manifest, ledger commit and .mrec record (generator/generate.go, builtin/custody_seal.go, builtin/ledger.go, security/record_file.go, security/record_crypto.go), and its public half was the key `--secure --signer-auth` trusts when --trusted-key is absent. One command line therefore gave opposite security verdicts depending on an environment variable. The policy guard missed it because it matched only Getenv-style selectors. Verifier: whoever controls the examiner's launch environment already has stronger levers (PATH), so this broke a reproducibility and policy promise rather than a privilege boundary.
evidence: key_bootstrap.go:23 `homeDir, err := os.UserHomeDir()`, then `filepath.Join(homeDir, ".mutant", "keys")`. CONFIGURATION_POLICY Rule 2 permits reading a foreign variable only where the value is observed, never obeyed. Verifier: changing USERPROFILE/HOME with t.Setenv changed both ResolveLocalKeyStoreDir and the key pair EnsureLocalSigningKeyPair returned. The fix (2026-09-28): TestTheKeystoreDoesNotFollowTheEnvironment failed first on Windows ('with HOME and USERPROFILE set to <temp> the keystore is <temp>\.mutant\keys: the environment chose it'). A first fix through user.LookupId still failed on Linux (WSL, CGO_ENABLED=0) for a uid missing from /etc/passwd (unshare --map-user=12345), because os/user's LookupId returns Current()'s answer for the caller's own uid and Current falls back to $HOME: the keystore was $HOME/.mutant/keys again. With the fix the same probe gave /home/<user>/.mutant/keys for the caller's own uid with HOME pointed elsewhere, and for uid 12345 the refusal 'the account database (/etc/passwd) has no entry for uid 12345'.
repro: Scratch build of 7aeee5a, PowerShell. (1) With $env:USERPROFILE=w\attackerHome, `mutant gen hello.mut --password-file pw.txt` bootstrapped keys under attackerHome\.mutant\keys and signed hello.mu. (2) With $env:USERPROFILE=w\victimHome, `mutant hello.mu --signer-auth --password-file pw.txt` printed `untrusted signer public key` / `event=signature_failed stage=secure-mode-verify action=terminate` and exited 1. (3) The same command with $env:USERPROFILE=w\attackerHome printed `hello from artifact` and exited 0.
impact: Whoever could set one inherited variable in the examiner's launch environment (a wrapper script, a scheduled task, a CI job) chose which key signs the case documents and which signer --signer-auth trusts, and the recorded command line showed none of it. The 'Production, no pinned signer yet' posture (SECURITY_RUNBOOK section 9) trusted whatever key that variable pointed at.
fix_proposal: Resolve the home directory from the OS account database rather than the environment, add os.UserHomeDir, os.UserCacheDir, os.UserConfigDir and os.TempDir to the policy guard, and state in CONFIGURATION_POLICY section 3 which inherited variables still affect behaviour. Fixed: ResolveLocalKeyStoreDir takes the home directory from accountHomeDir -- the process token's profile directory on Windows, os/user through libc on macOS, and on Linux /etc/passwd read directly (passwdHomeDir parses it as os/user does), because os/user built without cgo answers from $HOME for a uid the file does not list and LookupId returns that answer for the caller's own uid -- and refuses an account the database cannot answer for, or one without an absolute home. The guard now flags those four os functions, os.MkdirTemp/os.CreateTemp and ioutil.TempDir/TempFile with an empty directory, and, in files that build for Linux without cgo, user.Current/Lookup/LookupId, matched through import aliases; the allowlist gained display, scratch and regression categories. CONFIGURATION_POLICY section 3 lists every variable the runtime and the linked libraries still read (M26-NET-010, M26-NET-025 and M26-DAT-030 are the defects among them), and the runbook, the traceability doc, the deep dive, the quick reference and the LLD say where the keystore's home comes from.

title: The evidence read-only guard does not cover about ten evidence-reading files; a truncate of the evidence path in one passes the guard
claim: EVIDENCE_HANDLING_POLICY says the list covers "disk images and volumes ... deleted-file recovery" and that the guard "is what makes the assertion true" when case_manifest writes integrity.evidence_read_only:true. EvidenceReadOnlyFiles omits the Phase 2/3 evidence readers: builtin/filesystem_region.go (opens the image at :182), disk_image_extents.go (a custodyRecordOpen site), filesystem_deleted.go, filesystem_recover.go, filesystem_journal.go, filesystem_slack.go, filesystem_stream.go, filesystem_xattr.go, filesystem_verify.go and filesystem_report.go. A filesystem mutation in any of them is invisible to TestEvidenceCodeNeverWrites. Verifier: As stated. The doc already calls the hand-maintained list 'the one soft edge'. The defect is that its coverage sentence claims families the list omits, so the court-facing evidence_read_only:true is not backed for the Phase 2/3 filesystem files. No actual write to evidence exists today.
evidence: The list has 21 files. The only filesystem entries are disk_image_parsers.go, filesystem_parsers.go, table_parsers.go and fs_deleted_builtins.go. `ls builtin | grep filesystem_` shows filesystem_{capabilities,deleted,journal,parsers,recover,region,report,slack,stream,verify,xattr}.go. M26-CUS-020's verifier wrote that "the static AST guard (policy/evidence_guard_test.go) still backs the claim on the source side", which is not true for these files. Verifier: policy/evidence_policy.go:31-56 lists 21 files. filesystem_region.go, which opens the image at :182 with os.Open(path), is not on it, and neither are disk_image_extents.go, filesystem_{deleted,recover,journal,slack,stream,xattr,verify,report}.go. Repro in the scratch tree: I appended `func zzTruncEvidence(p string) error { return os.Truncate(p, 0) }` to builtin/filesystem_region.go and `go1.26.2 test ./policy -run TestEvidence` gave ok. The same line in builtin/archive.go gave FAIL with the EVIDENCE_HANDLING_POLICY message. Both files were restored. EVIDENCE_HANDLING_POLICY section 2 claims coverage of disk images/volumes and deleted-file recovery. Verifier's notes: TEST.01 has the same root: the list omits filesystem_region.go and filesystem_recover.go. DOC3.02 should survive because it gives the fuller file list, and TEST.01 should be a duplicate of it except for its separate syscall.Open mutator-set gap. repro: In the scratch copy I appended `func zzDoc3TruncateEvidence(path string) error { return os.Truncate(path, 0) }` to builtin/filesystem_region.go. `CGO_ENABLED=0 go1.26.2 test -count=1 -run TestEvidence ./policy/` gave `ok mutant/policy 0.502s`. Adding the same line to builtin/archive.go (a listed file) gave FAIL with the "read-only by construction ... See docs/EVIDENCE_HANDLING_POLICY.md" message. Both files were restored afterwards.
impact: The court-facing manifest claim evidence_read_only:true is guarded for only part of the evidence code. A patch that writes through the partition-offset opener, recovery, journal, slack or xattr paths would ship with the guard green.
fix_proposal: Add the missing files to EvidenceReadOnlyFiles, with allowlist entries for the examiner-output writes (filesystem_recover.go:1128 O_EXCL destination). Better, derive membership from the code: fail when a file calls custodyRecordOpen/At or os.Open on a builtin argument and is not on the list. Update the doc's coverage sentence to match. Regression test: TestEvidencePolicyCoversEveryEvidenceOpener: parse builtin/*.go and assert that every non-test file containing a custodyRecordOpen/custodyRecordOpenAt call, or a *_open builtin registration, appears in EvidenceReadOnlyFiles.

title: A password-quality control is traced as implemented, but no password policy exists; a 1-character password is accepted
claim: Row SEC-006, "Password quality policy required when explicit password mode is used", has status I/P and anchors security/kdf.go#L73 and generator/generate.go#L26, with tests "covered by generator path behavior and policy validation unit scope". Gap 4 asks for more coverage of the "generator password complexity rejection path". No password-quality check exists anywhere, and SECURITY_LLD 7.2 reads only "Easy memorable passwords". Verifier: The traceability matrix marks a password-quality control as (partly) implemented, and gap 4 asks for tests of a 'complexity rejection path', but no password policy exists and any non-empty password is accepted. LLD 7.2 suggests the lax policy is deliberate. So this is a documentation defect about a control that does not exist. It is not an enforcement regression: downgraded to S4 P2.
evidence: grep -rniE 'password.{0,20}(quality|complex|strength|policy|too short|weak)|ValidatePassword|minPasswordLen' --include=*.go finds nothing outside tests. The only checks are emptiness: kdf.go:47 `if len(password) == 0` and credential.go:298 "supplied an empty password". kdf.go:73 is the `KeyLen: DefaultKeyLen,` line of a struct literal. Verifier: Repro: pw1.txt = 'a'. `mutant gen weak.mut --password-file pw1.txt` exited 0, and `mutant weak.mu --password-file pw1.txt` printed 'weak ran' and exited 0. There is no quality check in the Go source. TRACEABILITY:44 SEC-006 says 'Password quality policy required' with status I/P, and its anchor kdf.go#L73 is the `KeyLen: DefaultKeyLen,` struct-literal line. SECURITY_LLD 7.2's whole body is 'Easy memorable passwords'. Verifier's notes: The owner needs to decide whether to implement a minimum or to mark SEC-006 not-implemented by decision.
repro: Scratch build: `Set-Content pw1.txt 'a' -NoNewline; mutant gen weak.mut --password-file pw1.txt` exited 0, and `mutant weak.mu --password-file pw1.txt` ran the program (exit 0).
impact: A reviewer using the traceability matrix believes artifact confidentiality rests on an enforced password policy. It rests on whatever the operator typed: Argon2id at t=1/64 MiB over a 1-character password.
fix_proposal: Either implement a minimum-length/entropy check in credential resolution for gen/release, or mark SEC-006 as not implemented by decision, delete gap 4, and replace LLD 7.2 with a sentence stating that no password policy is enforced. Regression test: If implemented: a main_test case that `mutant gen` with a 1-byte password file exits non-zero. If not: a docs test that SEC-006 does not carry an I status.

title: Six security documents say the audit stream is a no-op; since Phase 1 every security event goes into a hash-chained audit log installed at init
location: docs/SECURITY_LLD.md 13.3; docs/SECURITY_RUNBOOK.md 3.3; docs/SECURITY_LLD_TRACEABILITY.md section 5 item 7; docs/SANDBOX_DETECTION.md:178; docs/SECURITY_ANSWERS.md:178; docs/BINARY_ARTIFACT_SECURITY_DEEP_DIVE.md:144
claim: LLD 13.3 says: "Not implemented. `auditEvent(event, stage)` is called by every `Record*` counter function but its body discards both arguments." The RUNBOOK says "The audit stream is a no-op ... a run emits no audit lines". The ANSWERS, SANDBOX and BINARY_ARTIFACT docs repeat "`auditEvent` is a no-op", and TRACEABILITY 5.2 says "Audit stream ... no-op". The code does the opposite. Verifier: As stated. Nuance: the audit chain is in-memory and nothing is written to stderr or disk unless the script calls audit_write, so 'a run emits no audit lines' is literally true for stderr. The claim 'auditEvent is a no-op/discards its arguments' is false.
evidence: security/audit_sink.go:75-81: `func auditEvent(event, stage string) { sink := auditSink.Load(); if sink == nil { return }; (*sink).AuditEvent(event, stage) }`. builtin/audit.go:113-115: `func init() { security.SetAuditSink(&auditLog) }`, with a comment saying this is done in init so that every entry point that can execute a program gets it. auditChain.AuditEvent appends a hash-chained entry that audit_head / audit_write / audit_verify expose to scripts. Verifier: security/audit_sink.go:75-81 forwards to the installed sink, and builtin/audit.go init() calls security.SetAuditSink(&auditLog). Repro aud.mut, a plain run: audit_head() returned {entries: 2, recording: true, chain_complete: true, status: ok}, and audit_write('aud.log') wrote an 'algorithm: mutant-audit-1' chain document. The docs say no-op: SECURITY_LLD 13.3 ('Not implemented ... discards both arguments'), RUNBOOK 3.3, TRACEABILITY section 5 item 7, SANDBOX_DETECTION:178, SECURITY_ANSWERS:178, BINARY_ARTIFACT_SECURITY_DEEP_DIVE:144.
repro: Code reading: audit_sink.go:75-81 and builtin/audit.go:113-120 contradict each cited doc line directly. No run is needed for a doc claim.
impact: The operational runbook tells incident responders that no audit trail exists. The hash-chained, manifest-bound record of every debugger, sandbox, integrity and signature event, with audit_write(path) to export it, is exactly the evidence those triage steps need.
fix_proposal: Rewrite LLD 13.3 and RUNBOOK 3.3 to describe the AuditSink seam, the chain, and audit_head/audit_write/audit_verify. Correct the one-line mentions in the other four docs, and add audit_write to the RUNBOOK's first-10-minutes checklist. Regression test: A docs test that fails when any file under docs/ contains "auditEvent" together with "no-op" or "discards".

title: The traceability matrix does not trace: about 60 of its 76 line anchors land on blank lines, imports, braces or past end of file, and its test map names tests that do not exist

Verifier: I resolved every `../x.go#Lnn` link in SECURITY_LLD_TRACEABILITY.md: 95 link occurrences, 72 unique anchors. Most land on blank lines (main.go:118/165/180/578, runner.go:27/49/67/93, generate.go:80), imports (runner_test.go:13, vm_security_policy_test.go:11), braces (code.go:177, crypto.go:196, vm.go:662) or unrelated lines (vm.go:333 'newSize = fallback', main.go:714 help text). security_test.go#L349 is past EOF (the file has 340 lines). About 12-15 land on the named symbol (signatures.go:33/54, crypto.go:29, key_bootstrap.go:37/85, processscan_manager.go:7, processscan_windows.go:5, antidebug_weighting.go:3, security_test.go:101, main.go:329). SEC-013 says 'no dedicated CLI parsing tests yet', but main_test.go:59/1049/1088 hold TestExtractSecurityModeArg, TestContradictoryModeFlagsAreRejected and TestNonContradictoryFlagCombinationsAreLeftAlone. repro: In the scratch copy: grep -oE '\(\.\./[a-zA-Z_/]+\.go#L[0-9]+\)' docs/SECURITY_LLD_TRACEABILITY.md | sort -u, then sed -n "${line}p" on each target file. Output recorded above.
impact: A reviewer following a row to its evidence reaches an import statement or a closing brace. The matrix's I/T/C status column is asserted without a working pointer behind it, and three coverage claims are wrong in both directions: tests that do not exist, and tests reported missing that do exist.

Regenerate the test map from real test names, and drop the env-override and delay rows. Mark gap 3 and backlog 1 as done. title: Security documents still describe environment-driven controls that the configuration policy says were removed
claim: LLD 18.2 lists "Env-driven policy downgrades (`warn`/`delay`) can reduce enforcement" as a residual risk. LLD 16.2 names test defaults "(`terminate`, delay=0, audit=1)". TRACEABILITY SEC-010 gives its config surface as "mode + tamper response env", and its test map says "env override honored". PROCESS_INJECTION_DETECTION_LLD 3.1 lists a "Process protection env gate: security/const.go", and Sprint D says "Enable enforce mode behind env gate. [done]" and "Keep emergency kill-switch env var. [done via mode/off gate]". REMOTE_PROCESS_SCAN_DEEP_DIVE 5 step 1 says "Resolve config from env".
evidence: response_policy.go:129-139: ResolveTamperResponse depends only on securityDevModeEnabled() and secureMode. resolveTamperDelay() returns the constant 250 ms, not 0. security/const.go:35-53 holds only error values, with no gate. processscan_config.go: remoteScanConfigState is a package var written only by SetRemoteScanConfigForTesting, with no env read, which the same deep dive's section 2 states correctly. Verifier: Doc lines: SECURITY_LLD.md:955 'Env-driven policy downgrades (warn/delay) can reduce enforcement'; :932 '(terminate, delay=0, audit=1)'; TRACEABILITY:51 SEC-010 config 'mode + tamper response env'; :184 'env override honored'; PROCESS_INJECTION_DETECTION_LLD.md:44 'Process protection env gate: security/const.go', :706, :708; REMOTE_PROCESS_SCAN_DEEP_DIVE.md:106 'Resolve config from env'. Code: ResolveTamperResponse (response_policy.go:129-139) depends only on the securityDevMode package var (devlog.go:40) and secureMode. resolveTamperDelay returns the 250 ms constant. security/const.go has no gate. processscan_config.go has no env read. Verifier's notes: The auditor cited TRACEABILITY :48 for SEC-010. The row is at :51.
repro: Code reading against each quoted line (response_policy.go:12-20, 129-139, 199-201; security/const.go; processscan_config.go).
impact: Readers of the security design are told of env-var controls and risks that do not exist. That is the one kind of statement the configuration policy says must never be documented (RUNBOOK 1.1 rule 2), and it sends reviewers looking for an override path.
fix_proposal: Delete LLD 18.2 and correct 16.2 (delay 250, no audit setting). Change the SEC-010 config surface to "mode flags" and drop "env override honored". Remove the env-gate row and the Sprint D env items from the injection LLD, and change "Resolve config from env" to "Read remoteScanConfigState". Regression test: Extend the configuration guard's doc check: fail on the phrases "env gate", "env override", "env var" and "from env" in docs/ outside CONFIGURATION_POLICY.md and historical CHANGELOG entries.

title: SECURITY_LLD 7.4 says single-argument runs use the deterministic development key; default mode refuses instead
claim: Section 7.4 says: "`mutil.GetPwd()` ... Used when: Single-arg `.mut`/`.mu` convenience paths. `--dev` mode running `.mu` without explicit `-pwd`." The first case is false. Outside --dev, a single-argument run never falls back to the built-in key (main_test.go:611 TestDefaultModeNeverUsesTheDevelopmentKey). The second case names the removed `-pwd` flag. Verifier: As stated. The code is stricter than the doc. The doc also names the removed -pwd flag.
evidence: The only non-test caller of GetPwd besides the --dev path in main.go is repl/repl.go:393. SECURITY_ANSWERS.md:10-14 correctly says "Omitting a password is an error, not a fallback -- except under `--dev`". Verifier: SECURITY_LLD 7.4 (:375-385) says GetPwd is used for 'Single-arg .mut/.mu convenience paths' and '--dev mode running .mu without explicit -pwd'. Repro, stdin not a terminal: `mutant hello.mu` and `mutant hello.mut` both printed 'no password given and stdin is not a terminal ... or --dev to use the built-in development key' and exited 1.
repro: Scratch build, PowerShell, stdin not a terminal: `mutant hello.mu` and `mutant hello.mut` both printed "no password given and stdin is not a terminal, so there is nothing to prompt. Use --password-file <path> or --password-stdin ..., or --dev to use the built-in development key" and exited 1.

title: SECURE_NETWORKING's 'language gotchas' 1 and 2 do not reproduce: a ';' after a for block and inline composite literal arguments both work
claim: Gotcha 1: "No `;` after a `for (...) { }` block. A trailing semicolon there is parsed as an empty statement and fails (`no prefix parse function for ;`)." Gotcha 2: "Don't pass array/hash *literals* as call arguments alongside other arguments ... Passing a composite literal inline can corrupt an earlier argument." Neither happens at this commit, so the doc teaches workarounds for bugs that no longer exist and tells readers the language is unsafe in a way it is not. Verifier: As stated. SECURE_NETWORKING gotchas 1 and 2 do not reproduce at 7aeee5a, including in function-local and nested shapes. I did not check gotcha 3 (top-level return).
evidence: g1.mut `for (x in xs) { total = total + x; };` compiled and printed `g1 total 6`. g4.mut `f([1, 2, 3], "mid", {"n": 7})` printed `g4a 3|mid|7`; `h({"p": 10}, [1, 20])` printed `g4b 30`; `str_join(["a", "b", "c"], ",")` printed `g4c a,b,c`; `for (i in [1, 2]) { putln("loop", i); };` printed both iterations. Verifier: My own g1.mut has `for (...) { };` at top level, inside a function, and nested for-in-for with trailing semicolons. It compiled with `mutant run` and printed 'g1 total 6' and 'g1 fn 14' under the VM. My g2.mut passes array and hash literals inline next to local variables and nested calls, `f(x, s, [1,2,3,4], {"n": 7, ...})` and `g(g("first", [9,9]), {"z": g("x", [1])})`. It printed the correct '42|mid|4|7 / 43|p-q|2|42' and 'g2b first'. Both exited 0. Verifier's notes: Related to EX.07: the same stale 'semicolon after block' gotcha in the workshop docs, at a different site. Fix them together.
repro: Scratch build: `mutant run g1.mut --password-file pw.txt` then `mutant g1.mu --dev --password-file pw.txt`, and the same for g2.mut and g4.mut. All exited 0 with correct output.
impact: Readers are steered away from ordinary syntax (inline option hashes, the idiom every other doc uses) by a claim of silent argument corruption, which for a forensic language undermines trust in every result.
fix_proposal: Delete gotchas 1 and 2, or, if they reproduce under a specific engine or shape, state that shape exactly and link the ledger row. Re-check gotcha 3 (a top-level `return` printed its value and stopped, which looks intended) and either specify the misbehaviour or remove it. Regression test: Add g1/g4-style programs to the parity suite, so that if either bug returns a test fails rather than a doc silently becoming true.

title: Smaller false specifics in the security docs: a command_blocked counter, a delay clamp, 'compile-time constant' gates, 'gated' polymorph transforms, 'implemented' scan types, and the runner stage list
claim: (a) A `command_blocked` counter or event (LLD 13.1, RUNBOOK 2, ANSWERS 10). (b) The delay is "clamped to `[0..5000]` by `MinTamperDelayMs`/`MaxTamperDelayMs`" (LLD 4.2). (c) `antiTamperProbeEnabled` is "a compile-time `true`" or a constant (LLD 9.3, RUNBOOK 3.2, ANSWERS 6, TRACEABILITY 10.1). (d) "Advanced transforms ... Currently gated in config" (SECURITY_DIAGRAMS 6, SECURITY_ENHANCEMENTS 1 Partial-1). (e) processscan types "Status: implemented (with current fields in code)", listing SignalSource, ImagePath, ParentPID, SessionID, IsProtected, Source and SignalName (PROCESS_INJECTION 13.2). (f) Sandbox detection "is enforced in runner.Run at pre-execution stage" only (SANDBOX_DETECTION). No doc says the whole pre-execution pass is skipped under --compat/--dev. (g) "VM integrity probing and telemetry export" implemented (SECURITY_ENHANCEMENTS 1.8). Verifier: As stated: seven minor false specifics.
evidence: (a) telemetry.go:9-24 and SecurityTelemetrySnapshot have no command_blocked, and there is no CommandBlocked anywhere in the Go source. (b) MinTamperDelayMs/MaxTamperDelayMs are referenced nowhere but their declaration, and resolveTamperDelay() returns `DefaultTamperDelayMs * time.Millisecond`. (c) antitamper_probe.go:7 `var antiTamperProbeEnabled = true` with an exported setter at :9. (d) compiler/polymorphic.go:86-106 turns on InsertNOPs, MutateOpcodes, RandomizeConstants and InsertDeadCode at every level >= 1, and polymorphicSafeStagesEnabled() returns true. SECURITY_ANSWERS 7 is correct. (e) processscan_types.go: RemoteProcessTarget{PID, Name, Executable} and RemoteProcessSignal{Name, Detected, Weight, Confidence, Detail, Evidence}, with no SignalSource type. (f) runner.go:147-181: enforceAntiRev (debug, sandbox, process protection, remote scan) runs pre-decode in every mode and pre-execution only `if secureMode`. (g) ExportSecurityTelemetry has no caller. Verifier: (a) command_blocked appears in SECURITY_LLD:817, RUNBOOK:38 and ANSWERS:172, and in no Go file. (b) Min/MaxTamperDelayMs are referenced only at their declaration (response_policy.go:18-19); resolveTamperDelay returns the 250 ms constant unclamped, although LLD:130-131 says 'clamped'. (c) antitamper_probe.go:7 is `var antiTamperProbeEnabled = true` with exported setter SetAntiTamperProbeEnabledForTesting, yet LLD:541, RUNBOOK:66, ANSWERS:81, TRACEABILITY:243 and ENABLEMENT_LLD:20 say compile-time constant. (d) compiler/polymorphic.go getConfig enables all four stages at level>=1 and polymorphicSafeStagesEnabled returns true, but DIAGRAMS:119 and ENHANCEMENTS:38 say 'gated'. (e) processscan_types.go has no SignalSource, ImagePath or ParentPID, but PROCESS_INJECTION 13.2 calls those types 'implemented'. (f) SANDBOX_DETECTION:129-138 lists sandbox only at pre-execution, but runner.go runs enforceAntiRev pre-decode in every mode and pre-execution only in secure mode. (g) ExportSecurityTelemetry has no non-test caller. Verifier's notes: (c) matters most. The gate is a mutable package var with an exported setter that any Go importer can call, not a constant.
repro: Code reading at the cited lines. grep -rn 'MaxTamperDelayMs\|MinTamperDelayMs' --include=*.go returns only response_policy.go:18-19, and grep -rn 'command_blocked\|CommandBlocked' --include=*.go returns nothing.
impact: Operators search telemetry for an event that is never emitted. Reviewers believe the probe gate cannot be changed by an embedding host (it can, through an exported setter), and that bytecode is only lightly mutated.
fix_proposal: Correct each item. Rename SetAntiTamperProbeEnabledForTesting's docs to "exported; any Go importer can call it", or make it test-only via an internal package or export_test.go. Regression test: A docs test that every counter name in LLD 13.1 is a key of SecurityTelemetrySnapshot().

title: DISCLOSURE_POLICY section 8: the by-name refusal of a passphrase option exists only in case_key_*; record_open and record_seal answer 'unknown option'
location: builtin/case_key.go secretOptionsArg; its callers in custody.go, custody_seal.go, case_bundle.go, class.go, record.go, view.go

evidence: The run printed: `record_open: ERROR:record_open: unknown option "passphrase" (accepted: grant)`, `case_key_open: ERROR:case_key_open: a passphrase is not an argument. ...`, `record_seal: ERROR:record_seal: unknown option "passphrase" (accepted: default, sign, segment_size, source)`. Verifier: refusePassphraseOption is called only at case_key.go:85/215/357. Repro opt.mut: record_open printed 'unknown option "passphrase" (accepted: grant)' and 'unknown option "password" (accepted: grant)'; record_seal printed 'unknown option "passphrase" (accepted: default, sign, segment_size, source)'; case_key_open printed 'a passphrase is not an argument...'. DISCLOSURE_POLICY:318-321 states the by-name refusal generally.
repro: Scratch build: opt.mut with `let o = {"passphrase": "hunter2"};` passed to record_open("nothing.mrec", o), case_key_open("nothing.key", o) and record_seal("a.bin", "b.mrec", [], o). Compiled with `mutant run` and executed with --dev.
impact: Low. The option is still refused, but a grant recipient who tries to pass the grant passphrase to record_open gets the "misspelling" message the policy says it avoids.
fix_proposal: Call refusePassphraseOption from record_open, record_seal(_quantised), view_define and any disclose_* builtin that takes options. Or narrow the doc sentence to case_key_*. Regression test: A table test over every builtin with an options hash in the disclosure family, asserting the by-name refusal text for each of the four names. Fixed: secretOptionsArg (builtin/case_key.go) refuses the four names by name through refusePassphraseOption and then parses the options as formatOptionsArg does. Every builtin in the case_, class_, record_, view_ and disclose_ families that takes an options hash -- case_open, case_evidence, case_write, case_report, case_bundle, case_key_create/open/rotate, class_define, record_seal, record_seal_quantised, record_open, view_define -- reads its options through it, before checking any other argument. The test finds those builtins from the metadata, so a new one with an options hash is held to the rule without being listed; before the fix 40 of its 52 cases failed. DISCLOSURE_POLICY section 8 names the families.

title: Three examples print len() of a result hash as a count, and their goldens lock in the wrong numbers
claim: bin_sections, mem_find_pe and db_bfs each return a HASH (format/path/sections; candidates/confirmed/headers; nodes/edges). Each of these examples prints len() of that hash, which counts its keys. So the golden records 'section_count: 3' for a PE with 15 sections, 'mem_find_pe count: 3' for a dump with 1 candidate, and 'nodes reachable from the process: 2' for a BFS that reached 3 nodes. Verifier: As stated. The defect is in the examples only, not the builtins, so P2 rather than P1.
evidence: binary_triage_sections_entropy.mut:11 `putln("section_count:", len(sections));`. Its golden line 5 reads 'section_count: 3', while line 3 of the same golden reads 'num_sections: 15' and 13_hexeye.golden reads 'bin_sections -> 15 sections'. memory_scan_to_detection.mut:9 `putln("mem_find_pe count:", len(pe_hits), ...)` gives golden 'mem_find_pe count: 3', while memory_forensics_example.golden reads 'mem_find_pe: {candidates: 1, confirmed: 0, ...}'. incident_graph.mut:36 `putln("nodes reachable from the process:", len(reached));` gives golden 'nodes reachable from the process: 2'. Probe output: `type: HASH keys: [format, path, sections]` / `sections len: 15`; `pe type: HASH len: 3 candidates: 1`; `reached: {edges: [1, 2], nodes: [1, 2, 3]} len: 2 nodes: 3`. Verifier: zz/v1.mut in b4c/EX/tree: bin_sections(sample_win.exe) -> HASH, len 3, len(s["sections"]) 15; mem_find_pe(memory_dump.bin) -> {candidates:1, confirmed:0, headers:[...]} len 3; db_bfs(out) over a->b, a->c -> {edges:[1,2], nodes:[1,2,3]} len 2. The goldens record section_count: 3, mem_find_pe count: 3, nodes reachable: 2. The builtins are correct; the examples take len() of the result hash. Verifier's notes: The incident_graph BFS call uses a valid direction ("out"), so M26-TOOL-002 does not apply here.
repro: Scratch tree zz/p1.mut and zz/p2.mut (bin_sections / mem_find_pe / db_bfs, printing type_of, keys, len and the inner array length). Run with .\mutant.exe run zz\p1.mut --password-file pw.txt, then .\mutant.exe zz\p1.mu --dev --password-file pw.txt, and the same for p2. Output as quoted in evidence.
impact: The examples teach a counting idiom that gives wrong forensic numbers: a sections count off by 12, a PE-candidate count tripled, a reachability count short by one. The sweep's --golden check then turns these wrong numbers into the expected output, so a correct fix would fail the gate.
fix_proposal: Use len(sections["sections"]), pe_hits["candidates"] (or len(pe_hits["headers"])) and len(reached["nodes"]), and re-record the three goldens. Consider an mlsp rule that flags len() on a builtin whose declared return is ParamHash with fields. Regression test: go run ./cmd/sweep --golden on the three files, with goldens that read section_count: 15, mem_find_pe count: 1, nodes reachable from the process: 3. Optionally a sweep-side test that fails when a golden line 'X count: N' disagrees with the builtin's own count field. Fixed: len(sections["sections"]), pe_hits["candidates"] and pe_hits["confirmed"], and len(reached["nodes"]); the three goldens re-recorded. The mlsp rule for len() of a hash with declared fields is not built.
regression_test: go run ./cmd/sweep --golden on the three files: section_count: 15, mem_find_pe candidates: 1, nodes reachable from the process: 3

title: detect_suspicious_files skips unreadable paths silently and reports detected:false; threat_triage's golden records that as its answer
claim: detect_suspicious_files does `data, err := os.ReadFile(path); if err != nil { continue }`. A path that cannot be read (missing, locked, permission denied) drops out with no error and no note, and a list made only of such paths comes back {count: 0, detected: false}. threat_triage feeds it four bare names that exist nowhere ('invoice.pdf.exe', 'update.scr'...), with a comment promising double-extension detection, and its golden records 'suspicious findings: {count: 0, detected: false, hits: []}'. Verifier: As stated. Downgraded from S2 to S3: the script author supplies the paths, the failure comes from the environment (missing, locked or ACL-denied files) and cannot be forced by crafted evidence, and the result lists hits rather than stating that each file is clean. It is still a silent coverage gap that looks like 'nothing suspicious'. The name-only double_extension check is skipped along with the read.
evidence: builtin/detection.go:425-427 quoted above. threat_triage.mut:11-13: `// Suspicious-file heuristics: double extensions, magic/extension mismatch.` / `let files = ["invoice.pdf.exe", "report.docx", "update.scr", "photo.jpg"];` / `let sus, err = detect_suspicious_files(files);`. threat_triage.golden line 2: 'suspicious findings: {count: 0, detected: false, hits: []}'. Probe: missing paths gave `missing: {count: 0, detected: false, hits: []} err:` (no error), and the same name as a real 5-byte file gave `present: {count: 1, detected: true, hits: [{... reasons: [double_extension] ...}]}`. The double_extension test uses only the name, so the file's existence makes no difference to it. Verifier: builtin/detection.go:425-427 `data, err := os.ReadFile(...); if err != nil { continue }`. zz/v2.mut: detect_suspicious_files(["invoice.pdf.exe","update.scr","no/such/dir/x.pdf.exe"]) -> {count: 0, detected: false, hits: []}, err empty; the same name as a real 5-byte file (zz/invoice.pdf.exe) -> count 1, reasons [double_extension]. Neither metadata.go:2159-2163 nor CAPABILITY_REFERENCE.md:580 says unreadable paths are skipped. threat_triage.golden line 2 records the empty result. Verifier's notes: The ledger has nothing for this; M26-ART-026 is detect_injection. It is rooted in builtin/ (ART/BLT area).
repro: Scratch tree zz/p5.mut: detect_suspicious_files(["invoice.pdf.exe","update.scr","no/such/dir/x.pdf.exe"]) and detect_suspicious_files(["zz/invoice.pdf.exe"]) after printf hello > zz/invoice.pdf.exe. Output as quoted in evidence.
impact: A triage run over evidence the tool cannot read (a locked file on a live system, a wrong mount path, an ACL-protected file) reports 'nothing suspicious' with err empty, a wrong forensic answer that looks right. The shipped example teaches exactly that failure as the expected output. It is not in the ledger (ART-026 covers detect_injection only).
fix_proposal: Keep going past a file that cannot be read, but report it: add an 'unreadable' / 'skipped: [{path, error}]' array and a 'complete' flag, or return an error when no path could be read. Evaluate the name-only reasons (double_extension) even when the read fails. Fix threat_triage to write its fixture files first (as file_triage_report does) or use examples/data paths, and re-record the golden. Regression test: Builtin test: DetectSuspiciousFiles(["/nonexistent/invoice.pdf.exe"]) must not return {detected:false, count:0} with a nil error: it must name the path as unread (and flag double_extension). Plus sweep --golden on threat_triage with a golden showing at least the invoice.pdf.exe and update.scr hits.

title: The Lua file example prints 'lua_run_file ok' while its script fails, and the Lua files the docs call runnable point at paths that do not exist
claim: (1) lua_sample_patch.lua calls io.open, which the sandbox removes, on "examples/code.mut", which moved to examples/basics/. So the script always fails. (2) lua_run_file_example checks only err, never result["ok"], so it prints 'lua_run_file ok' over a failed run. The golden records that, which contradicts RUNTIME_INTEGRATION.md's own rule 'Always check err first, then result["ok"]'. (3) lua_http_server_example.go reads "examples/lua_sample_patch.lua" (the file is under examples/lua/), so the stub the docs name exits at once. (4) static_binary_parser.lua defaults to examples/data/sample.exe, which does not exist (the fixture is sample_win.exe), so it always returns its 'sample_read_failed' JSON.
evidence: lua_run_file_example.golden lines 3-4: 'lua_run_file ok' / 'result:  {error: builtin:lua_run_file:1: attempt to index a non-table object(nil) with key 'open' ... ok: false ...}'. lua_sample_patch.lua:1 `local f = io.open("examples/code.mut", "r")`. RUNTIME_INTEGRATION.md:234 'See examples/lua/lua_run_file_example.mut and examples/lua/lua_sample_patch.lua for a runnable version of this pattern', and :265 '(see examples/lua/lua_http_server_example.go for a runnable stub that serves examples/lua/lua_sample_patch.lua this way)'. `go1.26.2 run examples/lua/lua_http_server_example.go` from the root: 'failed to read examples/lua_sample_patch.lua: open examples/lua_sample_patch.lua: The system cannot find the file specified. exit status 1'. zz/p6.mut lua_run_file(static_binary_parser.lua): 'ok: true', result '{"metadata":{"format":"unknown",...,"byte_length":0,...' ending in error sample_read_failed. Verifier: zz/v3.mut: lua_run_file(lua_sample_patch.lua) -> ok:false (io is nil in the sandbox; examples/code.mut is also gone), err empty, while lua_run_file_example prints 'lua_run_file ok'. lua_run_file(static_binary_parser.lua) -> ok:true, result JSON error 'sample_read_failed' (DEFAULT_SAMPLE_PATH examples/data/sample.exe; only sample_win.exe exists). `go1.26.2 run examples/lua/lua_http_server_example.go` -> 'failed to read examples/lua_sample_patch.lua ... exit status 1'. RUNTIME_INTEGRATION.md:234 and :265 call these runnable. Verifier's notes: TEST.09 is a narrower report of part (1)+(2) of this finding (lua_run_file_example golden). EX.03 is the survivor; TEST.09 should be marked duplicate_of EX.03.
repro: Scratch tree: .\mutant.exe run examples/lua/lua_run_file_example.mut ...; run the .mu. go1.26.2 run examples/lua/lua_http_server_example.go (Start-Job with a 90 s timeout; it returned at once). zz/p6.mut as above.
impact: All four Lua artifacts the docs send a reader to fail, and the one with a golden reports the failure as success. That teaches the exact two-layer error mistake the docs warn about. The static_binary_parser.lua 'hand-rolled JSON' reference, cited three times in RUNTIME_INTEGRATION.md, only ever produces its failure JSON.
fix_proposal: Rewrite lua_sample_patch.lua to use mutant.read_file("examples/basics/code.mut") and return a string. Make lua_run_file_example (and lua_run_http_example) branch on result["ok"] as the docs show. Fix the path in lua_http_server_example.go to examples/lua/lua_sample_patch.lua. Point static_binary_parser.lua at examples/data/sample_win.exe. Re-record the golden. Regression test: sweep --golden on lua_run_file_example with a golden showing ok: true. A sweep- or example-level Go test that runs lua_run_file on every examples/lua/*.lua and requires result.ok and no 'read_failed' marker.

title: Three unmarked examples need a terminal or an artifact; their goldens record the refusal and the sweep counts them as verified
claim: code.mut and recur.mut read two numbers with gets(), and 05_timestomp_detection needs an NTFS $MFT at the hard-coded C:/evidence/$MFT. None carries a `// mutant:sweep needs-input` marker, although the marker's own definition covers 'an evidence image ... a passphrase typed at a terminal'. So the sweep runs them with no input, and their goldens record only the refusal. They count among the '75 of 124 examples printed exactly what their .golden file records'. Verifier: Partly right. code.mut and recur.mut have a deliberate, commented EOF branch ('gets() ... at end of input hands back an error object'), so their goldens do check the gets() EOF path. They are not doing nothing. The real defects are (a) the verified-example count includes programs that skip their real work, and (b) 05's golden depends on whether the host has C:/evidence/$MFT. Low impact.
evidence: code.golden: 'Enter first number: Enter second number: no input to read; this example needs a terminal'. recur.golden: 'Enter starting number: How many lines to print: no input to read; this example needs a terminal'. 05_timestomp_detection.golden: 'No $MFT at C:/evidence/$MFT' / 'Set MFT_PATH to a standalone $MFT or an NTFS image, then re-run.' workshop/README.md:109 calls 05 'the only file that needs a real artifact'. sweep/marker.go:44-46 defines ModeNeedsInput as needing 'an evidence image, a live network peer, a passphrase typed at a terminal'. The sweep --golden run reported all three 'run, reproducible; matches golden'. The 05 golden also depends on the host: on a machine that has C:/evidence/$MFT the output differs. Verifier: sweep --golden in the scratch tree: code.mut, recur.mut, 05_timestomp_detection.mut all 'run, reproducible; matches golden'; none carries a mutant:sweep marker. sweep/marker.go:44-49 defines needs-input to cover a terminal passphrase and host-dependent output. 05 hard-codes C:/evidence/$MFT, so its output changes on a host that has that file.
repro: In the scratch tree: .\sweep.exe --mutant mutant.exe --golden examples; the summary reads '75 of 124 examples printed exactly what their .golden file records' and the three are among them.
impact: The verified-example count is inflated by three programs that did none of their work, and the 05 golden holds a host path whose presence changes the output. This is the exact situation M26-EX-005 fixed for 33 other files.
fix_proposal: Mark all three `// mutant:sweep needs-input -- <reason>` and delete their goldens. If a runnable demo is wanted, give code/recur a non-interactive path, and point 05 at a shipped $MFT fixture (the usb_stick.img pattern). Regression test: Extend TestTheMarkedProgramsAreTheOnesWeExpect to include the three. Optionally a sweep check that fails --update-golden when output contains 'needs a terminal' / 'no input to read'.

title: Two host-reporting security examples are unmarked, while their siblings are needs-input for the same reason; one prints the whole process environment
claim: security_diagnostics_example and security_environment_report are marked needs-input because they 'report this machine's debugger and VM state, which differs from host to host'. security_quickcheck calls the same debug_status/sandbox_status/security_diagnostics and has no marker. system_forensics_example has no marker either, yet it prints the process list, the full process_env, open files and loaded modules of whoever runs it, and runs process_memory_scan on its own pid for 'malware'. Verifier: The inconsistent marking is real. The impact is overstated: scripts/release_gate.ps1:201 and release_gate.sh:147 run the sweep without -v, so gate logs do not capture the environment. Only a manual `sweep -v` or a direct run prints it. The self-scan hits are the M26-NET-007 mechanism.
evidence: security_quickcheck.mut:3-10 calls debug_status(), sandbox_status(), security_diagnostics(). security_diagnostics_example.mut:1 `// mutant:sweep needs-input -- reports this machine's debugger and VM state, which differs from host to host`. system_forensics_example.mut:9-10 `let env, err = process_env(); putln("process_env:", env, ...)` printed this host's whole environment (APPDATA, AI_AGENT, ANDROID_HOME, ...), and :24 `process_memory_scan(phash["pid"], "malware")` returned a list of hit addresses in the tool's own memory (the M26-NET-007 mechanism). The sweep ran both as 'run' (system_forensics 'output varies'; security_quickcheck 'reproducible; no golden' this run, flaky per M26-TOOL-008). Verifier: Only security_diagnostics_example.mut and security_environment_report.mut carry needs-input. security_quickcheck.mut calls the same debug_status/sandbox_status/security_diagnostics with no marker. system_forensics_example.mut has no marker. Sweep: both 'run, output varies; no golden' (exit status only). A direct run printed the full process_env (O:=..., AI_AGENT, ...) and process_memory_scan self-hit addresses.
repro: In the scratch tree: .\sweep.exe --mutant mutant.exe -v examples/security/security_quickcheck.mut, and run system_forensics_example.mu --dev directly.
impact: The markers are inconsistent, so the gate still runs host-dependent programs. `sweep -v` output and gate logs capture the full environment of the machine that ran them, including any tokens in env vars. The memory-scan line teaches that 'malware' was found in the analyst's own tool.
fix_proposal: Mark both needs-input with the siblings' reason. In system_forensics_example print counts or keys (e.g. len(keys(env))) rather than the environment, and scan another process or drop the self-scan until M26-NET-007 is fixed. Regression test: TestTheMarkedProgramsAreTheOnesWeExpect lists both. A sweep.Check rule: a program calling debug_status/sandbox_status/security_diagnostics/process_env/process_list must carry needs-input.

title: The memory fixture stores its shellcode as hex text, so every shellcode demo and golden records zero hits
claim: memory_dump.bin holds the ASCII characters '90909031c05068' where the x86 bytes 90 90 90 31 C0 50 68 (NOP sled + xor eax,eax; push eax; push) were clearly meant. mem_find_shellcode matches raw bytes, so both memory examples and detect_injection record 'no shellcode' as expected output, for a fixture that folder's README describes as shellcode/PE hunting. Verifier: The fixture is wrong as stated. The claim that a broken mem_find_shellcode would go unnoticed holds only for the example goldens: builtin/memory_forensics_test.go TestMemScanFindPEAndShellcode tests the positive path with its own fixture. examples/memory/README.md does not describe shellcode hunting. This is demo quality, so P3.
evidence: od of the fixture, offset 31: '39 30 39 30 39 30 33 31 63 30 35 30 36 38' = '90909031c05068'. memory_forensics_example.golden: 'mem_find_shellcode: [] err:' and 'mem_strings: [Memory-Snapshot, NOPNOP, 90909031c05068]'. memory_scan_to_detection.golden: 'mem_find_shellcode count: 0'. builtin/memory_forensics.go signatures {0x90,0x90,0x90}, {0x31,0xc0,0x50,0x68}. The probe with the same 31-byte prefix plus the real bytes gave `[{offset: 31, signature: 909090}, {offset: 34, signature: 31C05068}]`, and detect_injection then reported shellcode_hits: 1, matched xor_push. Verifier: od: memory_dump.bin offset 31 holds ASCII '90909031c05068'. zz/v7.mut: mem_find_shellcode(original) -> []; the same 31-byte prefix plus the real bytes 90 90 90 31 C0 50 68 (zz/mem_fixed.bin) -> [{offset: 31, signature: 909090}, {offset: 34, signature: 31C05068}].
repro: Scratch tree: head -c 31 examples/data/memory_dump.bin > zz/mem_fixed.bin; printf '\x90\x90\x90\x31\xc0\x50\x68\x00\x0d\x0a' >> zz/mem_fixed.bin; zz/p7.mut runs mem_find_shellcode on both files and detect_injection on the fixed one.
impact: The examples never show a positive shellcode result, so a broken mem_find_shellcode would still match its goldens: the golden for this path cannot fail. Readers learn that the demo 'finds nothing'.
fix_proposal: Regenerate memory_dump.bin with the real bytes (examples/data is -text, so bytes are kept), update fs_integrity_baseline's size/hash lines, and re-record the memory, detection and 13_hexeye goldens. Regression test: sweep --golden with memory goldens showing two shellcode hits. A Go test asserting mem_find_shellcode(examples/data/memory_dump.bin) is non-empty.

title: The workshop teaches two language gotchas that are no longer true: the nested-loop corruption and the 'semicolons after blocks' parse error
claim: Student-facing text tells students not to write a while or C-style for inside a for-in because it 'corrupts the outer iterator ("loop cursor was replaced on the stack")'. That was fixed in 14d4ea5 (compiler/compiler.go + vm/loop_nesting_test.go). RUN_SHEET_2H.md:228 also puts on 'a card on every desk' that omitting ';' after a block statement is a parse error. Blocks without the semicolon compile and run, and 09_revenant.mut's own `for (n in nums) { ... }` lines have none. Verifier: As stated. Note that the message 'loop cursor was replaced on the stack' can still appear via M26-CMP-003 (break/continue inside an expression operand), which is a different trigger from the one the tables describe. The semicolon half is the same misstatement DOC1.05 reports in LANGUAGE_REFERENCE/TUTORIAL, in different files. Priority P2 (S4 docs), not P1.
evidence: README.md:105 '| `while` / C-style `for` inside a `for…in` | `loop cursor was replaced on the stack` | use `for (i in range(a, b))` ...'. RUN_SHEET_2H.md:226 the same, :228 '| Semicolons after block statements | parse error | `if (c) { … };` and `let f = fn(){ … };` |'. 09_revenant.mut:198-204 'NOTE the inner loop spelling ... In this build, a C-style `for` or a `while` written directly inside a `for..in` body corrupts the outer iterator'. Probe zz/p3.mut (for-in holding both a while and a C-style for; an `if {}` and a `let f = fn(){...}` with no trailing ';') compiled and printed 'nested total: 66' (3 x (2 + 20), correct), 'no-semicolon if ok', 'no-semicolon fn ok 1'. Verifier: zz/v3b.mut: a while and a C-style for inside a for-in (at top level and inside a fn) -> 'nested total: 66' and 'in fn: 6' (both correct); `if (c) {...}` and `let f = fn(x){...}` with no ';' compile and run. Fixed by 14d4ea5 (compiler/compiler.go, vm/loop_nesting_test.go). README.md:105, RUN_SHEET_2H.md:226,228 and 09_revenant.mut:198-204 still teach the old behaviour. Verifier's notes: Related to DOC1.05 (semicolons) but not a duplicate: different files, and this finding's main half is the loop gotcha.
repro: Scratch tree zz/p3.mut: .\mutant.exe run zz\p3.mut --password-file pw.txt, then .\mutant.exe zz\p3.mu --dev --password-file pw.txt.
impact: The desk card makes students avoid ordinary constructs and teaches a false error. The revenant NOTE describes a defect of 'this build' that the shipped build does not have.
fix_proposal: Delete the nested-loop row in both tables and the NOTE in 09_revenant.mut (keeping `for (i in range(...))` is fine). Drop the semicolon row, or reword it to 'optional after a block'. Regression test: A docs test that fails if 'loop cursor was replaced' appears under examples/ while vm/loop_nesting_test.go exists. The semicolon claim has no test; review it by hand.

title: 13_hexeye teaches that a zero PE TimeDateStamp means 'somebody scrubbed it', on a Go binary whose linker always writes zero
claim: The lesson says the linker writes the build time and 'almost nobody removes it', and that '1970, or all zeroes -> somebody scrubbed it, which is itself a finding'. The file it walks, examples/data/sample_win.exe, is a Go binary: the same run prints bin_is_go -> true and TimeDateStamp 0. The Go linker hard-codes that field to 0, so for this sample the zero means 'built by Go', not tampering. Verifier: As stated. This also applies to other reproducible-build toolchains (for example MSVC /Brepro writes a hash rather than a time).
evidence: 13_hexeye.mut:158-159 '// The one field that is pure forensics: the linker wrote the build time here, as a plain Unix timestamp, and almost nobody removes it.' and :167-168 'built in the future, or 1970, or all zeroes -> somebody / scrubbed it, which is itself a finding'. 13_hexeye.golden: '+08  TimeDateStamp        : 0  = 1970-01-01 00:00:00 UTC' and 'bin_is_go     -> true'. go1.26.2 GOROOT src/cmd/link/internal/ld/pe.go:924 `fh.TimeDateStamp = 0`. Verifier: 13_hexeye.mut:158-168 text as quoted. 13_hexeye.golden: 'TimeDateStamp : 0 = 1970-01-01' and 'bin_is_go -> true'. go1.26.2 GOROOT src/cmd/link/internal/ld/pe.go:924 `fh.TimeDateStamp = 0`.
repro: Read the golden, then grep -n TimeDateStamp $(go1.26.2 env GOROOT)/src/cmd/link/internal/ld/pe.go.
impact: In the 'run this first' student exercise, students are taught to call a toolchain default an anti-forensic finding. That is a false-positive habit carried into real casework.
fix_proposal: Add a branch: when the timestamp is 0 and bin_is_go is true, print that Go (and other reproducible-build toolchains) write 0 by design. Otherwise keep the three cases. Re-record the golden. Regression test: sweep --golden on 13_hexeye with the reworded golden.

title: portscan_service README says Mutant has no import statement
claim: The README of the 'multi-file Mutant project' example says 'Mutant does not have an `import` statement; instead, a program composes other `.mut` files at runtime through builtins'. Mutant has import: examples/modules/main.mut:25 `import "lib/report.mut";`, docs/MODULES.md.
